Rashi on Niddah 3a:12:1.english: And how is it different from an alleyway - [The Gemara] raises this objection against Shammai.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:12:2.english: [It] renders impure retroactively - All pure items that were prepared in the alleyway.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:12:3.hebrew: עד שיאמר - עליו אדם: באותו היום בדקתי, ושוב אינו מטמא מאותו היום ולמפרע, אבל עד אותו יום הוא מטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:12:3.english: Until one says - [That is, until] a person says about it: "On that day I examined [it]," and it no longer renders [items] impure from that day retroactively, but up until that day, it renders [them] impure.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:12:4.hebrew: או עד שעת הכיבוד - אבל טהרות דקודם כיבוד טהורין, דחזקת ישראל בודקין מבואותיהן בשעת כיבודיהן, ואי הוה בההיא שעתא הוה מישתכח. אבל טהרות דלאחר כיבוד טמאות מספק, שמא לאחר כיבוד מיד נפל:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:12:4.english: Or until the time of the sweeping - However, ritually pure items [handled] before the sweeping are pure, for there is a presumption that Jews inspect their alleyways at the time of their sweeping, and had it been [there] at that time, it would have been found. But ritually pure items [handled] after the sweeping are impure out of uncertainty, lest it fell immediately after the sweeping.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:14:1.hebrew: מרגשת - שנט"ר בלע"ז. כלומר: יודעת בעצמה כשיוצא דם ממנה. והא מדלא ארגשה מאתמול, ודאי השתא בבדיקת עד נפק:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:14:1.english: Senses - *Sentir* in Old French. That is to say, she knows within herself when blood emerges from her. And since she did not sense [it] yesterday, it certainly emerged now during the examination with an examination cloth.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:16:1.english: And isn't there a mentally incompetent woman - Who does not have the understanding to sense [the flow].

Rashi on Niddah 3a:17:1.english: To exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Eliezer - It is in a mishna below (Niddah 7a).

Rashi on Niddah 3a:18:1.hebrew: והא איכא כתמים - הרואה כתם, דקיימא לן לקמן (נדה דף נו.), מטמאה למפרע, עד שתאמר בדקתי חלוק זה ולא היה בו כתם, או עד שעת כבוס, ולא אמרינן: אי נפיק מגופה הוה מרגשת:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:18:1.english: And behold, there are stains - A woman who finds a stain, as we maintain later (Niddah 56a), imparts impurity retroactively until [the time about which] she can say, "I examined this garment and there was no stain on it," or until the time of laundering; and we do not say, "If it had emerged from her body, she would have felt [it]."

Rashi on Niddah 3a:18:2.hebrew: לימא תנן כתמים דלא כשמאי - דכיון דאמר אשה מרגשת, אמאי טמאה? לימא: לאו מגופה הוה, הואיל ולא ארגשה:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:18:2.english: Shall we say that we learned [the mishna regarding] stains not in accordance with Shammai - For since [Shammai] says that a woman feels [the discharge], why is she impure? Let us say that it was not from her body, since she did not feel [it]!

Rashi on Niddah 3a:1:1.hebrew: מסוטה - דכתיב (במדבר ה) והיא נטמאה, איתקש טומאה לסוטה:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:1:1.english: From a sotah - As it is written (Numbers 5): "And she was defiled" — [ritual] impurity is juxtaposed to a sotah.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:20:1.hebrew: משמשת במוך - ממלאה אשה אותו מקום מוכין לשאוב את הזרע שלא תתעבר, ואינה נוטלתו משם אלא בשעת הצורך, ושמא מוך העמיד את הדם. ג' נשים משמשות במוך: קטנה, מעוברת ומניקה:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:20:1.english: [A woman who] engages in intercourse with an absorbent cloth - A woman fills that place [i.e., her vagina] with absorbent cloths to absorb the semen so that she will not become pregnant, and she does not remove it from there except at the time of need, and perhaps the absorbent cloth held back the blood. Three women may engage in intercourse with an absorbent cloth: a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:21:1.english: It contracts - And there are places for the blood to exit.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:22:1.hebrew: בין הני לישני - אשה מרגשת, ומעיקרא הוה אתי:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:22:1.english: Between these versions - [Namely:] "A woman senses [herself]," and "It would have come at the outset."

Rashi on Niddah 3a:22:2.english: To that version - [Namely,] "Establish a woman upon her presumptive status."

Rashi on Niddah 3a:2:1.english: And they treated her as definite - That she is forbidden to her husband until she drinks [the bitter water].

Rashi on Niddah 3a:3:1.english: A sotah in the public domain is pure - The public domain is not a place of seclusion.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:8:1.english: A basis for the matter - There is an indication of impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:8:2.hebrew: שהרי קינא לה ונסתרה - התרה בה אל תסתרי עמו, ונסתרה:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:8:2.english: For he warned her and she secluded herself - He warned her, "Do not seclude yourself with him," and she secluded herself.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:8:3.hebrew: מאי רגלים לדבר איכא - דליהוי חסר מקודם לכן? דילמא השתא הוא דחסר. וש"מ דקסבר ר' שמעון בשאר ספק טומאה דעלמא נמי ברה"י תולין, דהא אין רגלים לדבר:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:8:3.english: What basis for the matter is there - That it should have been deficient prior to this? Perhaps it is only now that it became deficient. And learn from this that Rabbi Shimon maintains that in other cases of ordinary doubt of ritual impurity as well, in a private domain [the status] is suspended, for there is no basis for the matter.

Rashi on Niddah 3a:9:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - אי מסוטה גמרי רבנן, הוה להו למימר ברה"ר טהור. אלא לאו מסוטה מצינן למגמר, דתחלת טומאה איתקש לסוטה, סוף טומאה לא איתקש. ואם כן, מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון דמטהר ברה"ר:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:9:1.english: And if you wish, say - If the Rabbis derive [it] from *sota*, they should have said [that] in the public domain it is pure. Rather, is it not that we cannot derive [it] from *sota*, as [only] the beginning of impurity was compared to *sota*, [whereas] the end of impurity was not compared [to it]? And if so, what is the reason of Rabbi Shimon, who declares [it] pure in the public domain?

Rashi on Niddah 3a:9:2.hebrew: גמר סוף טומאה - דהיינו טבילה, מתחלת מגע הטומאה:
Rashi on Niddah 3a:9:2.english: He derives the end of impurity - That is, immersion, [which he derives] from the beginning of contact with impurity.

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:12:1.hebrew: השרץ שנמצא במבוי - לשמאי פריך, דמטהר לגמרי:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:12:1.english: A creeping animal that is found in an alleyway - [The Gemara] poses the objection against Shammai, who deems [her] entirely pure.

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:13:1.hebrew: ושרצים דמעלמא - וא"ת: סיפא דקתני התם, כתם שנמצא בחלוקה מטמא למפרע עד שתאמר בדקתי את החלוק ולא היה בו כתם או עד שעת הכבוס — מאי איכא למימר? דהתם ליכא למימר דאיכא דם מגופה ומעלמא, דמשום דם דמעלמא אינו טמא אלא חלוק; ולקמן בפרקין (נדה דף ו.) נמי אמרינן: הרואה כתם מקולקלת למנינה! וי"ל, דהואיל ואם הכתם יבש הוא, ע"כ טמאה למפרע; ופעמים נמי, אף כשהוא לח, מוכיח דלא אתא השתא אלא על ידי שחייה או ע"י ריקוד, כדאמר בהרואה כתם (לקמן נדה נז:) — לא פלוג רבנן בכתמים:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:13:1.english: And creeping animals from elsewhere - And if you say: [Regarding] the latter clause, which teaches there: "A stain that was found on her garment defiles retroactively, until she can say: 'I checked the garment and there was no stain on it,' or until the time of laundering" — what is there to say? For there, one cannot say that there is blood from her body and [blood that came] from elsewhere, because on account of blood from elsewhere, only the garment is impure; and later in our chapter (Niddah 6a), we also say: "One who sees a stain is disrupted in her counting [of days]"! And one can say: Since if the stain is dry, she is perforce impure retroactively; and at times also, even when it is moist, [its location] proves that it did not come now, but rather through bending down or through jumping, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] HaRo'eh Ketem (below, Niddah 57b) — the Sages did not differentiate regarding stains.

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:14:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא טעמא דשמאי הואיל ואשה מרגשת בעצמה - נראה דלהאי לישנא נמי צריך טעמא דהעמד אשה על חזקתה, דאל"כ, כי קאמר מודה שמאי בשוטה וכן מודה שמאי במוך, וכי יטמאנה למפרע אף לחולין? והלא כל הנשים דיין שעתן לחולין, אף להלל! אלא הני טעמי לא איצטריך, אלא כי היכי דלא נעבד סייג בקדשים. [ומיהו לפי זה לא א"ש הא דאמר לקמן עשה סייג לדבריך, כיון דאיכא דהוה דם כו' לא הוה אלא סייג; ושמא טעמא דהגרושה אהני אף בשוטה לחולין. גיליון:]:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:14:1.english: And if you wish, say [that] Shammai's reason is: Since a woman senses herself - It appears that according to this version as well, the reason of "place a woman on her presumption [of ritual purity]" is also necessary. For if not so, when [the Gemara] says that Shammai concedes in [the case of] an imbecile, and similarly Shammai concedes in [the case of a woman who uses] an absorbent cloth, would he defile her retroactively even for non-sacred matters (chullin)? But don't all women [have the rule that] their time suffices for non-sacred matters, even according to Hillel! Rather, these reasons were not necessary except so that we should not enact a fence regarding consecrated items (kodashim). [However, according to this, that which [the Gemara] says below, "Enact a fence for your words," is not satisfactory: since [even] where there is [the reason that] "there was blood, etc.", it was only a fence; and perhaps the reason of the divorced woman is effective even for an imbecile regarding non-sacred matters. — Margin note]

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:14:2.hebrew: מרגשת בעצמה - פי', כשנעקר דם מן המקור; ומדלא הרגישה עד עכשיו, השתא הוא דחזאי. וא"ת: וכי בדקה עצמה ומצאה טמאה ולא הרגישה, מאי [טעמא דשמאי? נימא: כמו שלא הרגישה עכשיו, כך נימא שמא נעקר מאתמול ולא הרגישה?] וי"ל, דלא פלוג רבנן, הואיל ורוב פעמים מרגשת; דהא לטעמא ד"אם איתא דהוה דם מעיקרא הוה אתי", שוכבת אפרקיד מאי איכא למימר? אלא, לא פלוג רבנן. והא דקאמר "מודה שמאי בשוטה ובמוך", משום דהנהו חלוקות משאר נשים, ולא שייך למימר בהו לא פלוג רבנן. ורש"י פירש: מה שעכשיו לא הרגישה — כסבורה הרגשת עד הוא. וקשה: מאתמול נמי נימא, הא דלא הרגישה, אם שמשה — כסבורה הרגשת שמש הוא, ואמאי מטהרין למפרע? אלא, שמאי אית ליה דלעולם אשה מרגשת, ואינה חוששת בהרגשת עד ושמש, כמו שאינה חוששת בהרגשת מי רגלים:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:14:2.english: She senses within herself - Explanation: When blood is dislodged from the womb (makor). And since she did not sense [anything] until now, it is [only] now that she saw [it]. And if you say: If she examined herself and found [herself to be] ritually impure, yet did not sense [anything], what [is Shammai's reasoning? Shall we say: Just as she did not sense [it] now, so let us say [that] perhaps [blood] was dislodged yesterday and she did not sense [it]?] And one can say that the Rabbis did not differentiate [between cases], since most times she does sense [it]; for according to the rationale [given below], "If there were blood originally, it would have come out," [in the case of a woman] lying on her back (aferkid), what is there to say? Rather, the Rabbis did not differentiate. And that which [the Gemara] says, "Shammai concedes in [the case of] an imbecile and [a woman using] an absorbent cloth (mokh)" — [that is] because those [cases] are distinct from other women, and it is not applicable to say regarding them that the Rabbis did not differentiate. And Rashi explained: [As for the fact] that now she did not sense [it], she assumed it was the sensation of the examination cloth. And this is difficult: Yesterday as well, let us say that that which she did not sense, if she engaged in marital relations, she assumed [it] was the sensation of the [coital] organ! And why [then] is she deemed pure retroactively? Rather, Shammai holds that a woman always senses [the flow of blood], and she does not attribute [it to] the sensation of an examination cloth or [the] coital organ, just as she does not attribute [it to] the sensation of urine.

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:16:1.hebrew: מודה שמאי בשוטה - ואם תאמר: והא אין בו דעת לישאל? וי"ל, כגון אדם שנגע בה ורוצה לעסוק בקדשים, ואותו אדם יש בו דעת לישאל:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:16:1.english: Shammai concedes regarding an imbecile - And if you say: But doesn't [an imbecile] lack the capacity to be asked? And one can say: For example, [in a case where] a person touched her and wants to engage with consecrated items (kodashim), and that person has the capacity to be asked.

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:18:1.hebrew: והא איכא כתמים - פירוש: לשמאי, דאית ליה טעמא דהרגשה לטהר אף בקדשים, היה לנו לטהר כתמים אפי' מכאן ולהבא, דאית לן למימר: כיון דלא הרגישה, ודאי מעלמא אתי; כדאמר (לקמן נדה דף ה.) גבי תינוקת שלא הגיע זמנה לראות: אפילו סדינין שלה מלוכלכין בדם, אין חוששין לה, אימר בשוק של טבחים עברה ולאו אדעתה. אבל להלל לא קשה: כיון דאינו ברור לו טעמא דהרגשה לטהר בקדשים, אין לנו לתלות בכתמים ולומר דמעלמא אתי אפילו לחולין; דרגלים לדבר הוא דמגופה אתי, אפילו למפרע:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:18:1.english: But aren't there stains - The explanation is: According to Shammai, who maintains the reasoning of sensation (hargashah) to declare [items] pure even regarding consecrated items (kodashim), we should have declared stains pure even from now and onward, for we should say: Since she did not feel [a sensation], [the blood] certainly came from elsewhere (me-alma ata); as [the Gemara] says (below, Niddah 5a) regarding a young girl whose time to see [menstrual blood] has not [yet] arrived: "Even [if] her sheets are soiled with blood, we are not concerned for her; say [that perhaps] she passed through a butchers' market and was not aware of it." But according to Hillel, [this is] not difficult: Since the reasoning of sensation is not clear to him to declare [items] pure regarding consecrated items, we have no [basis] to attribute [the blood in the case of] stains and say that it came from elsewhere, even regarding non-sacred items (chullin); for there is circumstantial evidence (raglayim la-davar) that it came from her body, even retroactively.

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:1:1.hebrew: ושניהם לא למדוה אלא מסוטה - תימה, דהא רבנן מטמאין אף בר"ה משום דהוי תרתי לריעותא; אם כן, לא הוי ספק, ולא שייך זה לסוטה מידי! וכן בחבית, דהוי ודאי טבל לרבנן, דומיא דמקוה — הא לא גמרינן מסוטה אלא טומאה! ורבי שמעון נמי, דגמר חבית מטומאה — הא לא שייך מידי לסוטה! ואומר ר"ת, דלא קאמר הכי אלא לפרש דלא תקשי להו מסוטה. וטעמא דרבנן משום דהוי תרתי לריעותא, והוי ודאי ולא ספק; ולרבי שמעון הוי ספק, דלית ליה טעמא דהרי חסר לפניך, דהשתא הוא דחסר, וכנגד העמד מקוה בחזקת שלם איכא למימר העמד טמא על חזקתו; ולכך ברה"י תולין מדינא, ואע"ג דלא ילפינן מסוטה, ולכך בחבית נמי ספק. אבל ברה"ר מטהר, אע"ג דליכא חזקה, דמסוטה ילפינן, כדפי' לעיל; ובכל ספק טומאה אית ליה ברה"י תולין:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:1:1.english: And both of them derived it only from a sota - [This is] astonishing! For behold, the Rabbis declare [the items] impure even in a public domain (reshut ha-rabbim) because there are two points of impairment (tartei le-rei'uta); if so, it is not [treated as] a doubt, and this has nothing at all to do with a sota! And similarly regarding the barrel [of wine], which is definite tevel (untithed produce) according to the Rabbis, similar to the mikveh — surely we derive only [laws of] ritual impurity from a sota! And Rabbi Shimon as well, who derived [the law of the] barrel from ritual impurity — surely it has nothing to do with a sota! And Rabbeinu Tam says that [the Gemara] said this only to explain so that [the case of a] sota would not pose a difficulty to them: The reasoning of the Rabbis is that since there are two points of impairment, it is [treated as] definite and not a doubt; and according to Rabbi Shimon, it is a doubt, because he does not accept the reasoning of "behold, it is deficient before you" [to indicate that it was deficient all along], for [he holds that] it is only now that it became deficient, and counter to [the presumption of] "establish the mikveh on its presumption of completeness," one can say "establish the impure [person or vessel] on its presumption [of impurity]"; and therefore, in a private domain, they suspend [its status] by basic law, even though we do not derive it from a sota, and therefore regarding the barrel too, it is a doubt. However, in a public domain he declares [it] pure, even though there is no presumption [favoring purity], because we derive from a sota [that a doubt in a public domain is pure], as explained above; and in every [case of] doubtful ritual impurity, he holds that in a private domain they suspend [its status].

Tosafot on Niddah 3a:9:1.hebrew: גמר סוף טומאה מתחלת טומאה - תימה, דשפיר קאמרי רבנן דהתם איכא חזקת טהרה. וי"ל, דגמר מתחלת טומאה היכא דליכא חזקת טהרה — כגון ההיא דתנוק דפ' בתרא דקדושין (דף פ.), דאיכא רוב תינוקות מטפחין כנגד חזקת העיסה, ואינו רוב גמור והוי פלגא כנגד החזקה; ואילו היה בה דעת לישאל, מן התורה היה ברה"י טמא גמור וברה"ר טהור גמור, דגמרינן מסוטה. ורבנן, "התם איכא חזקת טהרה" — פי' כנגד רוב טיפוח, והוי ספק וגמרי מסוטה לטהר ברה"ר; אבל הכא, גברא בחזקת טומאה, והוי תרתי לריעותא והוי ודאי:
Tosafot on Niddah 3a:9:1.english: [Rabbi Shimon] derived the end of impurity from the beginning of impurity - It is puzzling, for the Rabbis argue well that there, there is a presumption of purity. And one can say that he derives [it] from [a case of] the beginning of impurity where there is no presumption of purity — such as that [case] of the child in the final chapter of Kiddushin (daf 80a), where there is a majority of children [who] pat [dough] opposing the presumption of the dough, and it is not an absolute majority, so it is [considered] half-and-half against the presumption; and if [the child] had the capacity to be questioned, by Torah law it would be completely impure in a private domain and completely pure in a public domain, as we derive from sotah. And the Rabbis [who say], "There, there is a presumption of purity" — the explanation is: [the presumption of purity stands] against the majority of patting, so that it becomes an [unresolved] doubt, and we derive from sotah to deem it pure in a public domain; but here, the person is in the presumption of impurity, so it is two [factors] to the detriment, and it is [treated as] definite [impurity].
